result.title: Autoregressive Decoding as a Martingale: Characterizing the Stochastic Dynamics of LLM Generation
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of language tasks. At their core, autoregressive LLMs are conditional probability models that learn to approximate the next-token distribution given the preceding context. Despite this probabilistic nature, the stochastic dynamics of autoregressive decoding have rarely been investigated from a rigorous probabilistic perspective. In this work, we define the per-step prediction error as the difference between the sampled token indicator and the model's conditional predictive distribution, and prove that the cumulative error process is a martingale with respect to the decoding filtration, implying that its conditional first-order moment is identically zero. Beyond this first-order property, we derive a closed-form expression for the second-order behavior of the martingale sequence: its predictable quadratic variation reduces to $\sum_t\left(1-p(y_t\mid y_{<t})\right)$, computable from realized token probabilities alone. This identity establishes a direct theoretical connection between sequence fluctuations and predictive uncertainty during autoregressive decoding. White-box experiments on Llama-3.x and Qwen2.5 families (1B to 72B parameters) verify that the empirically measured second-order moments closely match the theoretical predictions derived from our martingale analysis. These results provide a probabilistic framework for analyzing autoregressive LLM decoding, reveal intrinsic probabilistic fingerprints of different language models, and establish a rigorous mathematical foundation for LLM-generated text detection and uncertainty quantification.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把自回归解码的每步预测误差定义为采样 token 指示与模型条件预测分布之差，证明累积误差过程对解码滤波构成鞅，并导出可预测二次变差的闭式表达 Σ_t(1−p(y_t|y_<t))，在 Llama-3.x 与 Qwen2.5 上做了白盒验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本解码的鞅与二次变差刻画可能作为一种逐步骤不确定度累积的量具，可供核查 LVR 中基于不确定性的停止决策或 latent 推理轨迹波动分析；与视觉推理本身无直接关联。
